newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs off $0.50-$1.00 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs off $0.50-$1.00 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hogs were around $0.50 to $1.00 per cwt lower on Tuesday, weakened by sluggish demand and a pick-up in movement.
"There is good movement and not very good demand," one Indiana dealer said. "The IBP news is not helping."
IBP Inc said Monday it was cutting back production at its plants in Waterloo, Storm Lake, Perry and Columbus Junction, Iowa, as well as Madison, Neb. and Logansport, Ind.
"IBP's big announcement on cutbacks is having some effect. We also have a good run. It is cooler than it has been and our humidity is down," one Minnesota dealer said.
Early trade was reported in Indiana at $56.50 per cwt in the country and $58.00 at plants. USDA reported a top at plants in Indiana on Monday of $59.00.
In Minnesota there was trade at $55.50 to $56.00 in the country and $57.00 for plants, about $1.00 lower than prices paid for similar hogs on Monday.
"Movement is better than it has been and demand is just so-so," one Illinois dealer said, noting prices in his area looked set to be down $0.50 to $0.75 per cwt.
The IBP news was a less significant factor in Illinois as the company has no pork plants in the state, he added.
